                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1023,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"1. **URL-Scheme registrieren:** Deine App muss das URL-Scheme miataru:// in der Info.plist registrieren, damit sie von iOS geöffnet werden kann, wenn ein Nutzer einen passenden QR-Code scannt.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1031,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"Du kannst jetzt QR-Codes mit dem Schema &amp;#96;miataru://deviceid&amp;#96; scannen – wenn ein Nutzer so einen QR-Code mit der Kamera-App scannt und auf den Link tippt, öffnet sich deine App und zeigt direkt das „Gerät hinzufügen“-Sheet mit vorausgefüllter deviceID an.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1035,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"- Baue einen QR-Code mit Inhalt wie &amp;#96;miataru://DEINEDEVICEID&amp;#96;\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1040,
                  "content": "              \"file\": \"./.specstory/history/2025-07-18_19-25Z-qr-code-integration-for-ios-app.md\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1048,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"   Damit iOS deine App öffnen kann, wenn ein QR-Code mit einem Link wie &amp;#96;miataru://...&amp;#96; gescannt wird, musst du das URL-Schema &amp;#96;miataru&amp;#96; in deiner App registrieren.\""
                },

                  "lineNumber": 24173,
                  "content": "  \"plan\": \"# Implementation Plan: Mutual Navigation and Visitor History\\n\\n## Overview\\n\\nThis plan implements two features:\\n- **A) Mutual Navigation UI**: Detects when both devices are navigating to each other and shows visual indicators\\n- **B) Visitor History UI**: Lists devices that have accessed our location, with ability to add unknown devices\\n\\n## Architecture\\n\\n### A) Mutual Navigation Detection\\n\\n**Components:**\\n1. &amp;#96;MutualNavigationDetector&amp;#96;: ObservableObject that manages mutual navigation state\\n   - Polls &amp;#96;GetVisitorHistory&amp;#96; every 15-30s while navigation is active\\n   - Implements hysteresis logic (T_enter=60s, T_exit=90s)\\n   - Caches visitor history to avoid unnecessary UI updates\\n\\n2. Integration in &amp;#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&amp;#96;:\\n   - Track navigation active state (view is visible and polling)\\n   - Use &amp;#96;MutualNavigationDetector&amp;#96; to check if target device appears in visitor history\\n   - Update UI when mutual state changes\\n\\n**Files [... omitted end of long line]"

                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"- Add other devices by scanning their Miataru QR code.\\n- The QR tab offers one‑tap sharing, and the add‑device sheet guides scanning and rejects non‑Miataru codes.\\n\\n- The share sheet includes additional options, and email sharing attaches the QR image reliably.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&amp;#96; renders customizable QR codes using the &amp;#96;QRCode&amp;#96; package and supports &amp;#96;ShareLink&amp;#96; and &amp;#96;MFMailComposeViewController&amp;#96;.\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_AddDeviceView&amp;#96; validates the &amp;#96;miataru://&amp;#96; prefix from scanned codes before accepting an ID and allows manual entry with color selection.\\n\\n## Onboarding Flow\\n**For users:**\\n- A six‑step wizard guides through welcome, permissions, server URL, history settings, personal QR code display, and completion.\\n- Each step shows illustrations and contextual explanations; server selection validates custom HTTPS URLs, and completion flag controls whether the wizard reappears on next launc [... omitted end of long line]"

                  "content": "  \"plan\": \"# macOS Native Support Implementation Plan\\n\\n## Overview\\nTransform the miataru iOS/iPadOS app into a universal app that also targets macOS natively.                 {
                  "lineNumber": 954,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"| &amp;#96;message: Text(\\\"invalid_miataru_qr_code_error_text\\\"), //\\\"Der QR-Code muss mit 'miataru://' beginnen.\\\"&amp;#96; | L108 |\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1015,
                  "content": "              \"file\": \"./.specstory/history/2025-07-19_19-08Z-qr-code-scan-handling-for-app-launch.md\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1019,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"wenn ein nutzer den QR Code mit seiner camera app scannt wird diese die url miataru://deviceid aufrufen. Ich möchte dass meine App dann geöffnet wird und auf diese URL reagiert - also die deviceID extrahiert und den @iPhone_AddDeviceView.swift verwendet/vorausfüllt\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1023,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"1. **URL-Scheme registrieren:** Deine App muss das URL-Scheme miataru:// in der Info.plist registrieren, damit sie von iOS geöffnet werden kann, wenn ein Nutzer einen passenden QR-Code scannt.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1031,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"Du kannst jetzt QR-Codes mit dem Schema &amp;#96;miataru://deviceid&amp;#96; scannen – wenn ein Nutzer so einen QR-Code mit der Kamera-App scannt und auf den Link tippt, öffnet sich deine App und zeigt direkt das „Gerät hinzufügen“-Sheet mit vorausgefüllter deviceID an.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1035,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"- Baue einen QR-Code mit Inhalt wie &amp;#96;miataru://DEINEDEVICEID&amp;#96;\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1040,
                  "content": "              \"file\": \"./.specstory/history/2025-07-18_19-25Z-qr-code-integration-for-ios-app.md\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1044,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"die QR Codes enthalten ja eine URL nach dem schema: miataru://..... - ich möchte dass, wenn dieser qr code mit der ios kamera gescannt wird die App geöffnet wird von iOS und dann dieser Code als Device hinzugefügt werden kann\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1048,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"   Damit iOS deine App öffnen kann, wenn ein QR-Code mit einem Link wie &amp;#96;miataru://...&amp;#96; gescannt wird, musst du das URL-Schema &amp;#96;miataru&amp;#96; in deiner App registrieren.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1133,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"                message: Text(\\\"invalid_miataru_qr_code_error_text\\\"), //\\\"Der QR-Code muss mit 'miataru://' beginnen.\\\"\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1160,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"- &amp;#96;iPhone_AddDeviceView&amp;#96; integrates &amp;#96;CodeScanner&amp;#96; to scan &amp;#96;miataru://&amp;#96; QR codes, offers a color picker, and prevents duplicate IDs.\""
                },

              "file": "./Libraries/QRCode-main/README.md",
              "matches": [
                {
                  "lineNumber": 3,
                  "content": "A quick, stylish and beautiful macOS/iOS/tvOS/watchOS QR Code generator/detector library for SwiftUI, Swift and Objective-C."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 93,
                  "content": "* It's nice to have a simple drop-in component for displaying a QR code when you need it!"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 100,
                  "content": "* Generate a QR code without access to a UI."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 107,
                  "content": "* Add a logo to a QR code."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 110,
                  "content": "* Command line tool for generating qr codes from the command line (macOS 10.13+)."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 111,
                  "content": "* Basic qr code video detection (via importing &#96;QRCodeDetector&#96;)."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 129,
                  "content": "The core functionality for generating a nice QR code is found in the &#96;QRCode&#96; library."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 131,
                  "content": "If you want to use the qr code video detection, you'll need to import the &#96;QRCodeDetector&#96; library.  The reason for"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 136,
                  "content": "* For QR code generation, link against &#96;QRCode&#96;"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 137,
                  "content": "* For QR code video detection, link against &#96;QRCodeDetector&#96; "
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 172,
                  "content": "## Creating a QR Code"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 174,
                  "content": "You create a QR Code by creating an instance of &#96;QRCode.Document&#96;"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 229,
                  "content": "## Generating your QR Code"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 231,
                  "content": "&#96;QRCode.Document&#96; has many methods and styles for generating a QR Code."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 245,
                  "content": "### Set the QR code's encoded content"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 262,
                  "content": "The higher the error correction level, the larger the QR code will be."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 266,
                  "content": "&#96;QRCode&#96; supports a number of ways of 'designing' your qr code.  By default, the qr code will be generated in its traditional form - square, black foreground and white background. By tweaking the design settings of the qr code you can make it a touch fancier."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 270,
                  "content": "\tYou can style your QR code so much that it can no longer be read by readers."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 272,
                  "content": "\t\t1. Always check that your QR code can be read **at the size that it will be presented to users**. (hint: use your phone!)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 273,
                  "content": "\t\t2. Have good contrast between the QR Code and its background"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 281,
                  "content": "| shape  | The shape of each of the individual components within the QR code         |"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 282,
                  "content": "| style  | The fill styles for each of the individual components within the QR code  |"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 284,
                  "content": "You can individually specify the shape and fill style for each of the components of the QR code."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 286,
                  "content": "### QR code components"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 294,
                  "content": "## Styling your QR Code"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 311,
                  "content": "// Generate a CGPath object containing the QR code"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 317,
                  "content": "// Generate pdf data containing the qr code"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 323,
                  "content": "// Load a qr code from json"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 354,
                  "content": "The data shape represents how the 'pixels' within the QR code are displayed.  By default, this is a simple square, "
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 363,
                  "content": "You can provide an &#96;EyeShape&#96; object to style just the eyes of the generated qr code. There are built-in generators for"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 399,
                  "content": "You can specify a shape to be drawn when a data 'pixel' is _off_. This can be used to make your qr code prettier."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 400,
                  "content": "Just remember that the more embellishment you add to a QR code the more difficult it will be to read."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 431,
                  "content": "You can provide a custom fill for any of the individual components of the qr code."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 500,
                  "content": "The &#96;QRCode.Shadow&#96; class is used to apply shadows to a QR Code. The shadow is applied to the &#96;style&#96; component"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 505,
                  "content": "Adding heavy shadows can heavily adversely affect the ability to recognise the content of the QR code."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 599,
                  "content": "## Adding a logo to a QR code"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 601,
                  "content": "The &#96;QRCode.LogoTemplate&#96; class is used to define a logo on the QR code. "
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 606,
                  "content": "Adding a logo can heavily adversely affect the ability to recognise the content of the QR code. If you add a logo it's highly recommended to set the errorCorrection levels to &#96;.high&#96;."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 609,
                  "content": "After adding an image its important to verify that the qr code can be read (Most phone cameras can read qr codes)."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 610,
                  "content": "If the logo ends up covering more that 25% of the data, it is highly likely your QR code will have trouble being read by some readers."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 611,
                  "content": "Before reporting a bug about the qr code failing to be read, remove the image and retry. If the code can be read without the image it means your logo is too big."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 618,
                  "content": "The image and mask image should be the same size and square for the best results. Both the logo and the mask will be scaled to the final size of the QR code before application."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 631,
                  "content": "let doc = try QRCode.Document(utf8String: \"Adding a logo to a QR code using an image and a mask image\", errorCorrection: .high)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 644,
                  "content": "let doc = try QRCode.Document(utf8String: \"Adding a logo to a QR code using an image's transparency\", errorCorrection: .high)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 660,
                  "content": "The relative path represents the section in the QR code 'data' where the image is drawn. It represents a _relative_"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 661,
                  "content": "path (ie. x=0.0, y=0.0, width=1.0, height=1.0) within the bounds of the QR code."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 663,
                  "content": "x=0.0, y=0.0 represents the **top left** of the qr code."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 665,
                  "content": "For example, if you wanted to put a circle logo in the center of your qr code where the circle is "
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 666,
                  "content": "exactly 1/3 of the size of the QR code, then the path is defined as :-"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 676,
                  "content": "(note that a 1/3 mask will most likely render the qr code unreadable :-). "
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 678,
                  "content": "A 1/4 size rectangular logo in the lower right of the qr code would be :- "
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 688,
                  "content": "The mask path only affects the &#96;onPixels&#96; and &#96;offPixels&#96; within the QR code. Defining a logo that falls within the eye boundaries will be clipped. "
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 703,
                  "content": "// Define a rectangle mask within the bounds of the QR code. A centered square, 30% of the qr code size."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 721,
                  "content": "A round logo in the lower right of the qr code"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 741,
                  "content": "You can add a quiet zone around the outside of the QR code by setting &#96;additionalQuietZonePixels&#96; on the design object. This represents the number of pixels spacing are added around the outside of the actual QR Code."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 760,
                  "content": "You can specify a corner radius for your background fill on the style object, which is in fractional qr code data-pixel values."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 786,
                  "content": "There are a number of QRCode data formats that are somewhat common with QR code readers, such as QR codes "
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 789,
                  "content": "There are a number of built-in formatters for generating some common QR Code types. These can be found in the &#96;messages&#96; subfolder."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 808,
                  "content": "* The components of the qr code to include in the path (defaults to the standard QR components)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 811,
                  "content": "   * The pixels that are 'on' within the QR Code"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 812,
                  "content": "   * The pixels that are 'off' within the QR Code"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 815,
                  "content": "The components allow the caller to generate individual paths for the QR code components which can then be individually styled and recombined later on. "
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 817,
                  "content": "There are also extensions on &#96;CGPath&#96; to make it even easier to generate a &#96;CGPath&#96; from a qr code."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 829,
                  "content": "Generate an CGImage from the QR Code, using an (optional) design object for styling the QR code"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 835,
                  "content": "*(macOS only)* Generate an NSImage from the QR Code, using an (optional) design object for styling the QR code"

                {

                {
                  "lineNumber": 843,
                  "content": "### Generate a styled, scalable PDF representation of the QR Code"

                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 851,
                  "content": "### Generate a SVG representation of the QR Code"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 857,
                  "content": "Generate an SVG representation of the QR code."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 859,
                  "content": "### Add a QR Code to the pasteboard (macOS/iOS)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 873,
                  "content": "### Generate a text representation of the QR Code"
                },

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * iPad_RootView.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\nstruct iPad_RootView: View {\n    var body: some View {\n        TabView {\n            iPad_DevicesView()\n                .ignoresSafeArea(.container, edges: .top)\n                .tabItem {\n                    Label(\"devices\", systemImage: \"iphone.gen3.badge.location\")\n                }\n            iPad_GroupsView()\n                .ignoresSafeArea(.container, edges: .top)\n                .tabItem {\n                    Label(\"groups\", systemImage: \"person.3\")\n                }\n            iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView()\n                .tabItem {\n                    Label(\"qr\", systemImage: \"qrcode\")\n                }\n            iPhone_SettingsView()\n                .navigationViewStyle(.stack)\n                .tabItem {\n                    Label(\"settings\", systemImage: \"gear\")\n                }\n        }\n        .environmentObject(DeviceGroupStore.shared)\n        .environmentObject(RouteInfoState.shared)\n        .environmentObject(SettingsManager.shared)\n        .bottomAccessory(onTap: nil)\n        .ignoresSafeArea(.all)\n        .toolbarBackground(.clear, for: .tabBar)\n        .toolbarBackground(.clear, for: .navigationBar)\n        .toolbarBackgroundVisibility(.visible, for: .tabBar)\n        .toolbarBackgroundVisibility(.visible, for: .navigationBar)\n    }\n}\n\n#Preview {\n    iPad_RootView()\n}",

        "contents": "# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\n\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\n\n## App Navigation and Views\n**For users:**\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\n\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;iPhone_RootView&#96; constructs the &#96;TabView&#96; and hosts &#96;iPhone_DevicesView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_GroupsView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&#96;, and &#96;iPhone_SettingsView&#96;.\n- &#96;MiataruRootView&#96; selects platform‑specific root containers so iPad and Mac can embed their own navigation styles.\n- iPad supports opening device detail windows using a value‑based &#96;WindowGroup(for: String)&#96; and context menu/drag interactions.\n\n## Location Tracking\n**For users:**\n- Enable background and foreground tracking in *Settings* to share your location with a Miataru server.\n- The app sends updates even with the screen locked and records a log of recent updates.\n- Location sharing can store history on the server and works offline until network connectivity resumes.\n- Tracking accuracy, activity type, and sensitivity are configurable in *Settings*, and a \"Location Tracking Details\" page shows the last GPS and server updates.\n\n- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\n- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;LocationManager&#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &#96;MiataruAPIClient&#96;.",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

            "lineNumber": 6
          },
          {
            "text": "- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.",

          },
          {
            "text": "- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.",

          {
            "lineNumber": 11
          },
          {
            "text": "**For developers:**",
            "lineNumber": 12
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;iPhone_RootView&#96; constructs the &#96;TabView&#96; and hosts &#96;iPhone_DevicesView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_GroupsView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&#96;, and &#96;iPhone_SettingsView&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 13
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;MiataruRootView&#96; selects platform‑specific root containers so iPad and Mac can embed their own navigation styles.",
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "text": "- iPad supports opening device detail windows using a value‑based &#96;WindowGroup(for: String)&#96; and context menu/drag interactions.",
            "lineNumber": 15
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "text": "## Location Tracking",
            "lineNumber": 17
          },
          {
            "text": "**For users:**",
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "text": "- Enable background and foreground tracking in *Settings* to share your location with a Miataru server.",
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "text": "- The app sends updates even with the screen locked and records a log of recent updates.",
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "text": "- Location sharing can store history on the server and works offline until network connectivity resumes.",
            "lineNumber": 21
          },
          {
            "text": "- Tracking accuracy, activity type, and sensitivity are configurable in *Settings*, and a \"Location Tracking Details\" page shows the last GPS and server updates.",
            "lineNumber": 22

            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.",
            "lineNumber": 24

          {
            "text": "- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.",
            "lineNumber": 25

It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &#96;MiataruAPIClient&#96;.",

        "contents": "- Add other devices by scanning their Miataru QR code.\n- The QR tab offers one‑tap sharing, and the add‑device sheet guides scanning and rejects non‑Miataru codes.\n\n- The share sheet includes additional options, and email sharing attaches the QR image reliably.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&#96; renders customizable QR codes using the &#96;QRCode&#96; package and supports &#96;ShareLink&#96; and &#96;MFMailComposeViewController&#96;.\n- &#96;iPhone_AddDeviceView&#96; validates the &#96;miataru://&#96; prefix from scanned codes before accepting an ID and allows manual entry with color selection.\n\n## Onboarding Flow\n**For users:**\n- A six‑step wizard guides through welcome, permissions, server URL, history settings, personal QR code display, and completion.\n- Each step shows illustrations and contextual explanations; server selection validates custom HTTPS URLs, and completion flag controls whether the wizard reappears on next launch.\n\n**For developers:**\n- Platform‑specific containers (&#96;iPhone_OnboardingContainerView&#96;, &#96;iPad_OnboardingContainerView&#96;, &#96;Mac_OnboardingContainerView&#96;) embed the individual onboarding pages and update &#96;SettingsManager&#96; and &#96;UserDefaults.hasCompletedOnboarding&#96; as the user progresses.\n\n## Settings and Configuration\n**For users:**\n- Control tracking, data retention, server URL, device autolock, accuracy indicators, map type, zoom level, update interval, group zoom‑to‑fit, off‑screen arrows, auto‑refresh, reverse geocoding threshold, navigation mode, and route progress.\n- View location tracking details or replay the onboarding wizard.\n- Settings are grouped into tracking, app behavior, map configuration, and navigation sections for easier discovery.\n\n- All app preferences are also available in the system Settings app.\n- New options include: navigation route auto‑update, route progress visualization toggle, a global pulsing/shimmer switch for map markers, and off‑screen arrow visibility.\n- Bicycle transport mode was removed; existing values fall back to walking for directions and car icons where applicable.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;SettingsManager&#96; stores all preferences in &#96;UserDefaults&#96; and triggers side effects such as permission checks and auto‑refresh.",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {},

        "contents": "# miataru iOS App - Project Overview\n\n## 🎯 Project Purpose\nmiataru is a privacy-focused iOS application that enables users to track their device location, share it securely with trusted parties, and manage multiple devices and groups. The app prioritizes user privacy, battery efficiency, and cross-platform compatibility.\n\n## 🏗️ Architecture Overview\n\n### Technology Stack\n- **Frontend**: SwiftUI (iOS 18.0+)\n- **State Management**: ObservableObject pattern with @Published properties\n- **Data Persistence**: UserDefaults via SettingsManager; Application Support files for devices/groups\n- **Location Services**: CoreLocation framework (foreground and significant-change background)\n- **QR Code**: CodeScanner (scan), QRCode (generate)\n- **Platforms**: iPhone and iPad\n\n### Core Components\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nmiataruApp.swift (Entry Point)\n├── MiataruRootView (Main Navigation)\n├── OnboardingContainerView (User Setup)\n├── LocationManagers/\n│   └── LocationManager.swift\n├── SettingsManagers/\n│   └── App Settings/ (SettingsManager, thisDeviceIDManager, Settings.bundle)\n│   └── Devices/ (KnownDevice, KnownDeviceStore)\n│   └── Groups/ (DeviceGroup, DeviceGroupStore)\n├── views/\n│   ├── Common/ (Shared UI)\n│   ├── iPhone/ (iPhone-specific)\n│   ├── iPad/ (iPad-specific)\n│   └── Mac/ (onboarding previews only)\n└── Assets/ (Resources &amp; Localization)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Common Components Overview\n\n- Shared UI (&#96;views/Common/&#96;):\n  - &#96;ErrorOverlay&#96;, &#96;ViewModifiers&#96; (adaptive toolbars/navigation)\n  - Device &amp; group UI: &#96;DeviceRowView&#96;, &#96;GroupRowView&#96;, &#96;DeviceNameLabel&#96;, &#96;DeviceBatterySymbol&#96;\n  - Map UI &amp; helpers (&#96;views/Common/Map/&#96;): &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96;, &#96;PulsingAccuracyCircle&#96;, &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; (+ &#96;MapScaleBarViewModel&#96;), &#96;MapCompass&#96;, &#96;OffScreenDeviceArrow&#96;, &#96;OffscreenDeviceEdgeHelper&#96;, &#96;RouteGhostCalculator&#96;, &#96;RouteStyle&#96;, &#96;Shimmer&#96;\n- Data &amp; Caching:\n  - &#96;KnownDeviceStore&#96;, &#96;DeviceGroupStore&#96; (secure archiving under Application Support)",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * Mac_OnboardingContainerView.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\nstruct Mac_OnboardingContainerView: View {\n    @Binding var isPresented: Bool\n    @Binding var currentPage: Int\n    \n    private let pages: [AnyView] = [\n        AnyView(iPhone_1_OnboardingWelcomeView()),\n        AnyView(iPhone_2_OnboardingLocationPermissionView()),\n        AnyView(iPhone_3_OnboardingServerView()),\n        AnyView(iPhone_4_OnboardingLocationHistoryView()),\n        AnyView(iPhone_5_OnboardingQRcodeView()),\n        AnyView(iPhone_6_OnboardingDoneView())\n    ]\n    \n    var body: some View {\n        VStack {\n            TabView(selection: $currentPage) {\n                ForEach(0..&lt;pages.count, id: \\.self) { index in\n                    pages[index]\n                        .tag(index)\n                }\n            }\n            .tabViewStyle(PageTabViewStyle())\n            .indexViewStyle(PageIndexViewStyle(backgroundDisplayMode: .always))\n            \n            HStack {\n                if currentPage &gt; 0 {\n                    Button(\"Previous\") { currentPage -= 1 }\n                }\n                Spacer()\n                if currentPage &lt; pages.count - 1 {\n                    Button(\"Next\") { currentPage += 1 }\n                } else {\n                    Button(\"Finish\") {\n                        UserDefaults.standard.hasCompletedOnboarding = true\n                        isPresented = false\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            .padding()\n        }\n        .background(Color(.systemBackground))\n        .ignoresSafeArea()\n        .background(Color(.systemBackground).ignoresSafeArea())\n    }\n}\n\nstruct Mac_OnboardingContainerView_Previews: PreviewProvider {\n    @State static var isPresented = true\n    @State static var currentPage = 0",

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * iPhone_OnboardingContainerView.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\nstruct iPhone_OnboardingContainerView: View {\n    @Binding var isPresented: Bool\n    @Binding var currentPage: Int\n    \n    private var pages: [AnyView] {\n        [\n            AnyView(iPhone_1_OnboardingWelcomeView()),\n            AnyView(iPhone_2_OnboardingLocationPermissionView()),\n            AnyView(iPhone_3_OnboardingServerView()),\n            AnyView(iPhone_4_OnboardingLocationHistoryView()),\n            AnyView(iPhone_5_OnboardingQRcodeView()),\n            AnyView(iPhone_6_OnboardingDoneView(onFinish: {\n                UserDefaults.standard.hasCompletedOnboarding = true\n                isPresented = false\n            }))\n        ]\n    }\n    \n    var body: some View {\n        VStack {\n            TabView(selection: $currentPage) {\n                ForEach(0..&lt;pages.count, id: \\.self) { index in\n                    pages[index]\n                        .tag(index)\n                }\n            }\n            .tabViewStyle(PageTabViewStyle())\n            .indexViewStyle(PageIndexViewStyle(backgroundDisplayMode: .always))\n        }\n        .background(Color(.systemBackground))\n        .ignoresSafeArea()\n        .background(Color(.systemBackground).ignoresSafeArea())\n    }\n}\n\nstruct iPhone_OnboardingContainerView_Previews: PreviewProvider {\n    @State static var isPresented = true\n    @State static var currentPage = 0\n    static var previews: some View {\n        iPhone_OnboardingContainerView(isPresented: $isPresented, currentPage: $currentPage)\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * iPad_OnboardingContainerView.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\nstruct iPad_OnboardingContainerView: View {\n    @Binding var isPresented: Bool\n    @Binding var currentPage: Int\n    \n    private var pages: [AnyView] {\n        [\n            AnyView(iPhone_1_OnboardingWelcomeView()),\n            AnyView(iPhone_2_OnboardingLocationPermissionView()),\n            AnyView(iPhone_3_OnboardingServerView()),\n            AnyView(iPhone_4_OnboardingLocationHistoryView()),\n            AnyView(iPhone_5_OnboardingQRcodeView()),\n            AnyView(iPhone_6_OnboardingDoneView(onFinish: {\n                UserDefaults.standard.hasCompletedOnboarding = true\n                isPresented = false\n            }))\n        ]\n    }\n    \n    var body: some View {\n        VStack {\n            TabView(selection: $currentPage) {\n                ForEach(0..&lt;pages.count, id: \\.self) { index in\n                    pages[index]\n                        .tag(index)\n                }\n            }\n            .tabViewStyle(PageTabViewStyle())\n            .indexViewStyle(PageIndexViewStyle(backgroundDisplayMode: .always))\n        }\n        .background(Color(.systemBackground))\n        .ignoresSafeArea()\n        .background(Color(.systemBackground).ignoresSafeArea())\n    }\n}\n\n#Preview {\n    // Beispiel-Bindings für die Vorschau\n    @Previewable @State var isPresented = true\n    @Previewable @State var currentPage = 0\n    return iPad_OnboardingContainerView(isPresented: $isPresented, currentPage: $currentPage)\n}",

QRCode.Document(engine: QRCodeEngineExternal())\n\n\td.utf8String = \"https://www.swift.org\"\n\n\td.design.backgroundColor(CGColor(gray: 0, alpha: 0))\n\n\td.design.style.eye = QRCode.FillStyle.Solid(gray: 1)\n\td.design.style.eyeBackground = CGColor(gray: 0, alpha: 0.3)\n\n\td.design.shape.onPixels = QRCode.PixelShape.Square(insetFraction: 0.7)\n\td.design.style.onPixels = QRCode.FillStyle.Solid(gray: 1)\n\td.design.style.onPixelsBackground = CGColor(srgbRed: 1, green: 1, blue: 1, alpha: 0.3)\n\n\td.design.shape.offPixels = QRCode.PixelShape.Square(insetFraction: 0.7)\n\td.design.style.offPixels = QRCode.FillStyle.Solid(gray: 0)\n\td.design.style.offPixelsBackground = CGColor(srgbRed: 0, green: 0, blue: 0, alpha: 0.3)\n\n\td.design.style.background = QRCode.FillStyle.Image(CGImage.named(\"Apple_Swift_Logo\"))\n\n\treturn d\n}()\n\nstruct ContentView: View {\n\tvar body: some View {\n\t\tTabView {\n\t\t\tScrollView(.vertical) {\n\t\t\t\tVStack {\n\t\t\t\t\tPixelBackgroundColorsView()\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\t.frame(maxWidth: 100000)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t.tabItem { Text(\"basic\") }\n\n\t\t\tItemView()\n\t\t\t\t.tabItem { Text(\"3d\") }\n\t\t}\n\t\t.padding()\n\t}\n}\n\nstruct ContentView_Previews: PreviewProvider {\n\tstatic var previews: some View {\n\t\tContentView()\n\t}\n}\n\n// -\n\nstruct PixelBackgroundColorsView: View {\n\tvar body: some View {\n\t\tVStack {\n\t\t\tText(\"A logo with an overlaid QRCode.\")\n\t\t\tText(\"Note: The Eye color must match the on pixel color\")\n\t\t\tQRCodeDocumentUIView(document: doc1)\n\t\t\t\t.frame(width: 300, height: 300)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nstruct PixelBackgroundColorsView_Previews: PreviewProvider {\n\tstatic var previews: some View {\n\t\tPixelBackgroundColorsView()\n\t}\n}\n\n\n////",
